principles: Prefer Koala managed-asset repair commands over manual edits.
Keep this chore scoped to the reported drift only.
Make the verification observable from terminal commands.
drivers: `koala check` currently blocks clean convergence because `.gitignore` is stale.
The expected change is limited to two runtime ignore patterns.
Story process must preserve auditability and avoid unrelated repo churn.

options.name: run-koala-check-apply
pros: Uses the official managed asset sync path
Matches the remediation printed by `koala check`
cons: Must still inspect the diff to ensure only `.gitignore` changed

options.name: manual-gitignore-edit
cons: Bypasses the managed asset repair path
More likely to drift from template expectations

options.name: leave-drift-as-advisory
cons: Leaves `koala check` noisy and undermines convergence hygiene

rationale: Use the official Koala managed asset sync because this is exactly the safe drift category that `koala check --apply` is designed to repair, then verify the resulting diff.

preMortem.trigger: Managed assets include additional stale files.
preMortem.mitigation: Inspect `git status` and `git diff --stat`; revert/stop if anything besides `.gitignore` changes.

preMortem.scenario: `koala check` still reports drift after apply.
preMortem.trigger: Template expectations changed or apply did not merge the runtime block.
preMortem.consequence: User still sees the original warning.
preMortem.mitigation: Capture the failure and do not mark CHK-001 done until drift is resolved.
